description:
Programme or Project Overview

Leiden University invites applications for a post-doctoral researcher working on agent-based modelling of Pleistocene landscape connectivity in Europe. The project simulates how Pleistocene environments connected and disconnected habitats and populations across the continent, informing debate in palaeoanthropology, archaeology and palaeoclimate research.

The postdoc will design and implement agent-based models that couple reconstructions of Pleistocene climate, vegetation and topography with movement and subsistence behaviour, and will run systematic simulation experiments across glacial and interglacial conditions. Results feed into European research collaborations on human-environment dynamics in deep time.

Candidate profile

Applicants hold a PhD in archaeology, palaeoecology, computational geography or a related discipline, with demonstrable experience in agent-based modelling, GIS and handling large palaeoenvironmental datasets. Strong programming skills are essential. The appointment is a salaried postdoctoral contract under the CAO-NU collective agreement, and the working language is English.

Highlights

  • Agent-based modelling of Pleistocene landscapes
  • Palaeoclimate and palaeoenvironment data integration
  • Simulation experiments across glacial cycles
  • GIS and spatial analysis in deep-time contexts
  • Collaboration in European research networks
  • Salaried postdoc under the CAO-NU agreement

About Leiden University

Leiden University, founded in 1575, is the oldest university in the Netherlands and a member of the League of European Research Universities (LERU). Its seven faculties in Leiden and The Hague cover humanities, law, social and behavioural sciences, medicine, science, archaeology and governance. Doctoral candidates at Leiden are salaried employees under the CAO-NU collective agreement rather than fee-paying students, which makes its PhD positions fully funded by design. All academic vacancies, including PhD and postdoctoral roles, are advertised on the university's dedicated careers portal.
